newsitem.title: UK: Albright condemns renewed IRA violence.
newsitem.headline: Albright condemns renewed IRA violence.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Wednesday condemned IRA guerrillas for resuming violence in Northern Ireland and said President Clinton remained committed to the search for peace in the British-ruled province.

Albright, who is on her maiden overseas trip as secretary of state, was speaking to reporters after talks with Prime Minister John Major, Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind and Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Patrick Mayhew.

"We have strongly condemned the renewal of IRA terrorist attacks and we will continue to support the efforts of the British and Irish governments and the political parties in Northern Ireland to move forward with the peace process," she said.

Albright said she backed the British government's insistence on the need for the Irish Republican Army to call a new ceasefire before its political arm, Sinn Fein, could join multi-party talks on Northern Ireland's future.
"We think it is very important that there be a credible ceasefire," she said.

Earlier Major told Albright he hoped the U.S. administration would continue to use its influence on the various parties in Northern Ireland. Albright told him she was "dismayed" by the resumption of IRA violence, according to Major's office.
IRA guerrillas have carried out a 28-year war to reunite Northern Ireland with Ireland.

Britain and Ireland, who are trying to ease tension between the province's pro-British majority Protestants and Irish minority Catholics, say the guerrillas must abandon violence to win a voice in peace talks.
Last week a British soldier was shot dead at a checkpoint near the frontier with Ireland and the IRA was widely blamed.
The guerrillas, who have made no comment on the shooting, say they will not consider a ceasefire before Britain has a new government. A British general election must be called by May.
